answer.notes:
Answer: 13600000000000000 wei (0.0136 ETH).

How it was computed. The brief's definitions pin the source to eth_getLogs over the pinned blocks decoded with the Seaport ABI, and no marketplace API was used. OrderFulfilled does not index the NFT contract, so instead of pulling every Seaport log in the window I took the equivalent and much cheaper route: every ERC-721 Transfer of the collection in the window (19 logs, 17 transactions), then the receipt of each of those transactions, then every OrderFulfilled log emitted by Seaport 1.5 or 1.6 inside them. This is complete: a Seaport fill of an ERC-721 of this collection necessarily transfers that token, so it necessarily appears in that Transfer set. topic0 was derived from the signature OrderFulfilled(bytes32,address,address,address,(uint8,address,uint256,uint256)[],(uint8,address,uint256,uint256,address)[]) and equals 0x9d9af8e38d66c62e2c12f0225249fd9d721c54b83f48d9352c97c6cacdcb6f31.

Totals over the window: 17 OrderFulfilled fills touching the collection, all 17 qualifying (exactly one ERC-721 item of the collection, no other NFT, every payment leg in ETH or WETH). Nothing was dropped for a bundle, an ERC-1155, or a non-ETH token. Prices ran from 0.0136 ETH to 0.05 ETH; the four next-lowest were 13724000000000000, 13818000000000000, 14400000000000000 and 14600000000000000 wei, so the minimum is not a lone outlier.

The minimum is a Seaport 1.6 bid fill in block 26025131, transaction 0xdf89e1ad5fb24617f83a3dc9b549991774e78ac1ccb061b691ae3b2097480d0f, log index 668: offer is a single WETH item of 13600000000000000 wei; consideration is token 4422 of the collection plus two WETH fee items (136000000000000 and 680000000000000). Per the brief's bid rule the price is the offer amount, 13600000000000000, which is the fee-inclusive gross. The lowest listing fill was 13724000000000000 wei, so the choice of the gross bid amount over a fee-net figure does not change the ordering of the bottom of the book.

Why the recipe is panel. The brief sets "evidence": "panel", and the catalogue's chain recipes cannot express this computation in any case: it is a minimum, not a sum or a rank, over a decoded dynamic ABI structure, and the collection is not an indexed topic of OrderFulfilled. The recipe therefore names the primary source and the exact query that reproduces the figure from public RPC data alone; no indexer, no API, no hand correction.

Endpoints used: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com for the logs and receipts (eth_chainId 1, closing block hash matched the pin), https://rpc.mevblocker.io/fast for an independent confirmation of chain id and the closing block hash. Log ranges were fetched 2000 blocks at a time and would have been halved on any refusal; none was refused.

definitions.bid price: offer item is native ETH (itemType 0) or WETH (itemType 1, 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2): price is that offer amount, gross, before the WETH fee items in the consideration are deducted, which is what 'fees included' means on this side.
definitions.denomination: wei, with 1 WETH counted as 1 ETH = 1e18 wei; ETH and WETH fills are pooled into one price series and no exchange rate is applied.
definitions.listing price: offer item is the collection's ERC-721: price is the sum of every consideration amount, fees and royalties included, and only when every consideration item is itemType 0 (native ETH) or itemType 1 with token 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2 (WETH). A consideration in any other token disqualifies the fill.
definitions.qualifying fill: an OrderFulfilled log from Seaport 1.5 (0x00000000000000adc04c56bf30ac9d3c0aaf14dc) or 1.6 (0x0000000000000068f116a894984e2db1123eb395), topic0 0x9d9af8e38d66c62e2c12f0225249fd9d721c54b83f48d9352c97c6cacdcb6f31, whose offer and consideration together hold exactly one NFT item and that item is itemType 2 (ERC-721) of 0x9c51a3cb5094b26aa1dcb380f3dc7e1a7c681c2d. Any log with a second NFT item of any type, or an ERC-1155 item, is dropped.
definitions.single offer item: the brief prices a listing fill by its one offer item and a bid fill by its one offer item, so only fills whose offer array has exactly one element are priced; no fill in this window had a longer offer array, so the rule excluded nothing.
